sections.title: Modeling Forces in the Real World

i_can_designs.evidence_job: Construct a force diagram for one identified object in a real-world situation, showing only forces acting on that object with appropriate directions and labels.
avoid_structures: selected-response presented as evidence that the student drew/constructed a diagram
generic diagram route without an executable response surface
i_can_designs.i_can: I can draw a force diagram for an object in a real-world situation.
i_can_designs.notes: Designed from the exact Unit 1 Assessment Plan target. Structures and representations are fit-driven, not quota-driven.

i_can_designs.evidence_job: Determine whether the forces on the modeled object are balanced or unbalanced and connect that judgment to zero or nonzero net force.
formula_relationships: Balanced forces imply F_net = 0; unbalanced forces imply F_net ≠ 0.
avoid_structures: diagram-free task when the mapped evidence is diagram interpretation
i_can_designs.i_can: I can decide whether the forces are balanced or unbalanced.
i_can_designs.notes: Designed from the exact Unit 1 Assessment Plan target. Structures and representations are fit-driven, not quota-driven.

i_can_designs.evidence_job: Explain how nonzero net force changes motion, diagnose an incorrect force explanation, and revise the explanation using accurate physics vocabulary and model reasoning.
formula_relationships: Net force direction indicates the direction of the change in motion; F_net = 0 corresponds to unchanged velocity.
avoid_structures: selected-response labeled as full evidence of a written critique/revision
i_can_designs.i_can: I can explain how the net force affects the object’s motion and critique an incorrect force explanation and revise it using physics vocabulary.
i_can_designs.notes: Designed from the exact Unit 1 Assessment Plan target. Structures and representations are fit-driven, not quota-driven.
